name: Viracopos International Airport
before:
Campinas's airport, 20 km south west of downtown Campinas but 82 km north west of São Paulo itself, beside the Bandeirantes-Anhanguera highway.

The booking code is the thing to understand, and it catches people out. Viracopos has two codes that behave differently in reservation systems. VCP is part of the São Paulo multiple airport system alongside Congonhas and Guarulhos, so a flight filed as VCP appears when someone searches for São Paulo. CPQ is the city code for Campinas, and a flight filed that way appears as Campinas instead. The same airport, two different search behaviours. It works much like New York, where JFK, LaGuardia and Newark all answer to NYC even though Newark is in another state.

So a client who books what a system called São Paulo may land 82 km away from the city. Quote the transfer explicitly.

The airport is operated by Aeroportos Brasil, and its name was officially settled in its present form on 6 January 1987.
after:
Campinas's airport, 20 km south west of downtown Campinas but 82 km north west of São Paulo itself. For a client bound for São Paulo, quote the road transfer explicitly.

The airport is operated by Aeroportos Brasil. Its official name, Viracopos-Campinas International Airport, was set by law on 6 January 1987.

claims.inAfter: The airport is operated by Aeroportos Brasil.
claims.note: Checked for a 2025 or 2026 change of operator: none found. Infraero's 2025 report (it looks ahead to 2026) still lists Viracopos Aeroportos Brasil as the company running the airport, with Infraero holding 49 per cent; it adds that the re-bidding (relicitação) of the concession was closed and that ANAC set up a negotiating commission with the Ministry of Ports and Airports and the Attorney General's office, still under way. Worth re-checking in 2027. The operator's own site (viracopos.com) could not be reached all evening: the proxy reported 'remote connection failure' three times and the browser tool got 502.

IATA's location-code directory can only be read through its own site search, which the sweep does not use, and no airline, operator or regulator page read tonight says how VCP is grouped. Worth checking by hand in a GDS: if VCP does sit under SAO, this is the most useful thing an agent can know about the airport.

claims.wasBefore: CPQ is the city code for Campinas, and a flight filed that way appears as Campinas instead.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and OurAirports casts doubt on it: it attaches CPQ to Campinas's small Campo dos Amarais airfield (SDAM), not to Viracopos. The sources disagree, so it goes.
